submitted.rationale: Index 34 (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.17, V 0.43) gave the highest photocurrent measured, 12.6 µA. Its XRD matches monoclinic BiVO4 (strongest peak at Q≈2.04 Å⁻¹). Its composition is close to Bi:V = 1:1 with low Cu, the classic photoanode region under 2.72 eV light.

rejected.reason: V-rich (Bi 0.18, V 0.66): 3.4 µA, lower than index 34
Slightly Bi-rich (Bi 0.43, V 0.39): 0.98 µA, a sharp drop, so photocurrent peaks near Bi:V = 1:1
Not measured. CuBi2O4 is a p-type photocathode, and the Cu oxides have small predicted gaps (CuO 0.3 eV, Cu2O 1.6 eV), so the region is unlikely to work as a photoanode

consultations.verdict: Weakly supportive. MEGNet puts the HSE gaps of V2O5 (2.83 eV) and Bi2O3 (2.34 eV) near or below the 2.72 eV photon energy, and Cu2O and CuO are low-gap absorbers. The XRD of index 34 has its strongest peak at Q=2.04 Å⁻¹, which matches monoclinic BiVO4 (121). BiVO4 is the known photoanode in this system, so a composition near Bi:V = 1:1 with low Cu is the prior best.

Mildly supportive. Depending on fidelity, MEGNet puts the V2O5 gap at 2.1–2.8 eV, so a V2O5 secondary phase can absorb at 2.72 eV and may form a heterojunction with BiVO4. Index 32 (Bi 0.18, Cu 0.16, V 0.66) tests the V-rich, low-Cu side, as an alternative to the stoichiometric BiVO4 region already measured (index 34, 12.6 µA).

Mildly supportive. MEGNet gives Bi2O3 a GLLB gap of about 2.3 eV, below the 2.72 eV photon energy, so moving slightly Bi-rich shouldn't cost absorption. The measured trend also favours more Bi: index 32 (Bi 0.18) gave 3.4 µA and index 34 (Bi 0.40) gave 12.6 µA. Index 281 (Bi 0.43, Cu 0.18, V 0.39) continues that trend while staying close to BiVO4 stoichiometry.
